title: How Precious Are Your Thoughts
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: God gave careful thought to forming you, his thoughts toward you are for good, and he bent all his thought on your salvation.
exhortation: What does God think about? What does he give his focused attention to? What does the Almighty of the universe ponder? Most of us probably never wonder what God's thoughts are, because we're endlessly concerned with our own. I know I am. But step back for a moment and think about what is on God's mind. The verses just before this one tell us a few things.

First, he gave thought to you and how you were formed. Verse 13 says, "You knitted me together in my mother's womb." The world is constantly attacking your body: look a different way, alter your appearance. There must be billions of dollars spent on people being told they need to change how they look. The Bible says no. You were formed by the purposeful, thoughtful creation of the Almighty.

Second, God's thoughts toward you are for peace and for good. Jeremiah 29:11 says, "For I know the plans I have for you, declares the Lord, plans for welfare and not for evil, to give you a future and a hope." And what happens when our thoughts become God's thoughts? Isaiah 26:3 tells us: "You keep him in perfect peace whose mind is stayed on you." When your mind is on God's thoughts, your mind has peace and your life has peace.

Third, God's thoughtfulness creates. He created you and the universe and all creation, so a mind that ponders God is a mind full of new works and building. And finally, in verse 24, we are led in the way everlasting. When God's thoughts become our thoughts, we are led toward eternity, toward a purpose and a mission beyond earthly concerns.

And when God lost the creation he had knit together in the womb and formed out of the dust in Adam, when it was lost at the fall, he bent all of his thought on salvation. He spared no cost for redemption. Think of Jesus asking if there was any other way. God's answer was, in effect: I have given this my deepest thought, and the path must be the cross. God focused his immeasurable energy on our salvation, and after counting the cost, he did it anyway. He sent Jesus to the cross to redeem us so that we might commune with him. That is worth pondering this morning.
prayer: Lord, what a beautiful picture as we remind ourselves that you knew our names and everything about us before the foundation of the world. You knit us together in our mothers' wombs. It's a mystery we can't explain, but it shows your love and care for us.

As we ponder your sacrifice on the cross, as we gaze on your wounds and the path you walked, carrying the cross we deserved to carry, receiving the lashes we deserved, dying the death we should have died so that we might be restored to you: what an amazing sacrifice, and what an amazing gift we have in Christ. I pray we would remember that today and take hope and joy and comfort in it. In Jesus' name, amen.
